title: Grape clafoutis
subtitle: a baked custard pudding with whole grapes set in a light eggy batter
excerpt: Grape clafoutis is a baked egg and cream batter set around whole seedless grapes in a buttered dish. The batter is similar to a thick crepe batter: milk, cream, eggs, flour, and sugar, poured around the fruit and baked until set and lightly puffed. It comes out of the oven puffed and deflates as it cools, which is normal.
sourceNotes: Clafoutis originated in the Limousin region of France, where it was traditionally made with black cherries. The name comes from the Occitan dialect word clafir, meaning to fill. The dish is documented in French regional cooking from at least the nineteenth century. Variations using other fruit are technically called flaugnarde in French, though clafoutis is widely used for all versions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten warm from the oven or at room temperature on the day it is made. The batter can be made up to 2 hours ahead and kept refrigerated.

content.text: Grape clafoutis is a baked custard with whole grapes set inside it. The batter is a thin mix of eggs, flour, milk, cream, and sugar, whisked smooth and poured over the fruit in a buttered dish. It puffs up as it bakes and sinks back as it cools; serve while still slightly warm and just set in the centre.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Butter a shallow ovenproof dish generously, then scatter a tablespoon of caster sugar over the butter and tilt to coat. Tip out the excess.

Whisk the eggs and remaining caster sugar together until pale. Add the vanilla, then sift in the flour and whisk until smooth. Gradually whisk in the milk and cream until you have a thin, smooth batter. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Spread the grapes in a single layer in the prepared dish. Pour the batter over the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the clafoutis is set at the edges and still has a slight wobble in the centre. A skewer inserted 5 cm from the edge should come out clean.
Remove from the oven and leave for 10 minutes. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

attrs.problem: Clafoutis very rubbery and dense after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid overbaking; the clafoutis sets firmer as it cools so should come out with a gentle wobble.
attrs.fix: The centre should jiggle when the dish is moved at the end of the baking time. Remove it then and let it finish setting in the residual heat of the dish.

attrs.problem: Grapes all floating to the top of the batter
attrs.avoid: Avoid very wet or juicy grapes that release moisture into the batter and rise.
attrs.fix: Dry the grapes thoroughly before adding them. Patting them with kitchen paper removes surface moisture. Very large grapes can be halved to help them stay in place.
